attractions.name: Grand Palace, Bangkok
attractions.desc: The former royal residence, its ornate spires and gilded surfaces still used for state ceremonies despite the king no longer living there. Wat Phra Kaew within the complex houses the revered Emerald Buddha, actually carved from jade, dressed in seasonal robes changed by the king three times a year. Modest dress covering shoulders and knees is strictly enforced.

attractions.name: Old City temples, Chiang Mai
attractions.desc: Wat Phra Singh and Wat Chedi Luang sit within the moated old town, their weathered brick chedis and gold-leafed Buddha images reflecting centuries as the capital of the former Lanna kingdom. A generally slower, more relaxed pace than Bangkok makes it a favorite base for longer stays. The surrounding mountains add cooler air and hiking options rarely found in the south.

attractions.name: Phi Phi Islands
attractions.desc: Limestone cliffs rising dramatically from turquoise water, best reached by longtail boat from Krabi or Phuket for day trips or overnight stays. Maya Bay, made famous by the film The Beach, now enforces visitor limits and closed hours to allow coral recovery. Snorkeling and diving here rank among the most scenic in Thailand.

attractions.name: Ayutthaya
attractions.desc: Ruins of the former Siamese capital, destroyed by Burmese invasion in the 18th century, its brick chedis and Buddha statues, including one famously entwined in tree roots, scattered across a well-preserved historical park. It served as one of the most important trading cities in Southeast Asia before its fall. It's an easy day trip from Bangkok by train or boat.

attractions.name: Railay Beach
attractions.desc: A peninsula accessible only by boat due to surrounding limestone cliffs, making it feel like an island despite being connected to the mainland. It's become a major destination for rock climbers, with hundreds of bolted routes directly above the beach. Several distinct beaches here range from lively to nearly deserted, all within a short walk.

attractions.name: Wat Arun, Bangkok
attractions.desc: The Temple of Dawn sits directly on the Chao Phraya River, its central spire decorated with thousands of pieces of colorful Chinese porcelain that catch the light distinctively at sunset. Steep steps allow a partial climb for river views. A short ferry crossing from the older side of the river makes it an easy addition to a day exploring the Grand Palace area.

itinerary.label: Days 1–3
itinerary.title: Bangkok & Ayutthaya
itinerary.desc: The Grand Palace, riverside temples, and a day trip to the ruined former capital.
itinerary.cost: Grand Palace entry ~500 THB; a day-trip minivan to Ayutthaya runs 200–400 THB.
itinerary.food: Eat at least one meal at a street-food stall in Chinatown (Yaowarat) — some of the best pad thai in the city.

itinerary.label: Days 4–5
itinerary.title: Chiang Mai
itinerary.desc: Old city temples and an ethical elephant sanctuary in the surrounding hills.
itinerary.cost: Ethical elephant sanctuary day trips run 2,000–3,000 THB; temple entries are mostly free or under 50 THB.
itinerary.food: Try khao soi, the region's signature coconut curry noodle soup — best found at small local shops, not tourist restaurants.

itinerary.label: Days 6–9
itinerary.title: Krabi & Phi Phi
itinerary.desc: Island-hopping by longtail boat, with time to dive or just swim.
itinerary.cost: A full-day longtail island-hopping tour runs 800–1,500 THB including snorkel gear.
itinerary.food: Grilled seafood by the kilo at any beachfront stall in Ao Nang is hard to beat for the price.

goodToKnow.tipping: Not obligatory but small tips are appreciated in restaurants
goodToKnow.safety: Very safe overall; usual caution with beach parties and scooter rentals
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Domestic flights, overnight trains, and ferries cover the country well
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Most international flights land at Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi (BKK); budget carriers often use Don Mueang (DMK) instead — check which one before booking onward transport

faq.q: How long can I stay in Thailand without a visa?
faq.a: 30 days for most Western passport holders as of September 2026 (reduced from 60), extendable once for a further 30 days. You'll also need to complete a Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online within 72 hours of arrival.

faq.q: Which Bangkok airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Suvarnabhumi (BKK) handles most international full-service airlines; Don Mueang (DMK) is used mainly by budget carriers. They're about 45 minutes apart by taxi, so check your onward connections before booking.
Yes, overall very safe — petty scams around tourist sites and caution with scooter rentals and beach parties are the main things to watch, not serious crime.

faq.q: Do I need to tip in Thailand?
faq.a: Not obligatory anywhere, but rounding up or leaving small change in restaurants is appreciated and increasingly common in tourist areas.

daysReason: 9 days covers Bangkok, Chiang Mai, and one island group at a comfortable pace — this is the range most first-time visitors land on. 7 works if you drop one stop; 12–14 lets you add Chiang Rai or a second island.
visa: Visa-free entry was cut from 60 to 30 days as of 15 September 2026 for most Western passport holders, extendable once by 30 days. A digital arrival card (TDAC) must also be completed within 72 hours of arrival — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Grande Palácio, Banguecoque
attractions.desc: A antiga residência real, com os seus pináculos ornamentados e superfícies douradas ainda usadas em cerimónias de estado apesar de o rei já não viver lá. O Wat Phra Kaew dentro do complexo alberga o venerado Buda de Esmeralda, na verdade esculpido em jade, vestido com túnicas sazonais trocadas pelo rei três vezes por ano. É estritamente exigido vestuário que cubra ombros e joelhos.

attractions.name: Templos da Cidade Velha, Chiang Mai
attractions.desc: Wat Phra Singh e Wat Chedi Luang situam-se dentro da cidade velha rodeada de fosso, com os seus chedis de tijolo desgastados e imagens de Buda douradas a refletir séculos como capital do antigo reino de Lanna. Um ritmo geralmente mais lento e relaxado do que Banguecoque torna-a uma base preferida para estadias mais longas. As montanhas circundantes acrescentam ar mais fresco e opções de caminhada raramente encontradas no sul.

attractions.name: Ilhas Phi Phi
attractions.desc: Falésias calcárias erguendo-se dramaticamente de água turquesa, alcançáveis por barco longtail a partir de Krabi ou Phuket para excursões de um dia ou estadias durante a noite. A Maya Bay, famosa pelo filme A Praia, aplica agora limites de visitantes e horários de encerramento para permitir a recuperação do coral. O mergulho e o mergulho com snorkel aqui contam-se entre os mais cénicos da Tailândia.

attractions.name: Ayutthaya
attractions.desc: Ruínas da antiga capital do Sião, destruída pela invasão birmanesa no século XVIII, com os seus chedis de tijolo e estátuas de Buda, incluindo uma famosamente envolvida em raízes de árvore, espalhados por um parque histórico bem preservado. Foi outrora uma das cidades comerciais mais importantes do Sudeste Asiático antes da sua queda. É uma excursão fácil de um dia a partir de Banguecoque, de comboio ou barco.

attractions.name: Praia de Railay
attractions.desc: Uma península acessível apenas por barco devido às falésias calcárias circundantes, fazendo-a sentir como uma ilha apesar de estar ligada ao continente. Tornou-se um importante destino de escalada, com centenas de rotas equipadas mesmo acima da praia. Várias praias distintas aqui vão de animadas a quase desertas, todas a curta distância a pé.

attractions.name: Wat Arun, Banguecoque
attractions.desc: O Templo do Amanhecer situa-se mesmo junto ao Rio Chao Phraya, com o seu pináculo central decorado com milhares de peças de porcelana chinesa colorida que captam a luz de forma distinta ao pôr do sol. Escadas íngremes permitem uma subida parcial para vistas sobre o rio. Uma curta travessia de ferry desde o lado mais antigo do rio torna-o um acrescento fácil a um dia a explorar a zona do Grande Palácio.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–3
itinerary.title: Banguecoque e Ayutthaya
itinerary.desc: O Grande Palácio, templos à beira-rio, e uma excursão de um dia à antiga capital em ruínas.

itinerary.label: Dias 4–5
itinerary.title: Chiang Mai
itinerary.desc: Templos da cidade velha e um santuário ético de elefantes nas colinas circundantes.

itinerary.label: Dias 6–9
itinerary.title: Krabi e Phi Phi
itinerary.desc: Saltos entre ilhas de barco longtail, com tempo para mergulhar ou simplesmente nadar.
